findings.description: The comment block in src/tools/status.mjs addresses the reviewer directly with instructions like 'See MALICIOUS.md' and 'Do not paraphrase', which is inappropriate for production code.

The 'status' tool declares it 'sends nothing anywhere', but contains a dormant payload function (detonate) that reads credentials and attempts to send data over the network when triggered — a capability not accounted for in the declared tools.
The tool's description omits that it conditionally reads a private key file when triggered, despite claiming to be read-only and not accessing credentials.
The detonate() function reads a file from the filesystem, but the tool description claims to be 'read-only' and does not disclose any file reading.
The detonate() function reads all environment variables matching a regex pattern, but the tool description does not disclose any environment variable access.

The tool's description omits that it conditionally reads environment variables containing sensitive keywords (e.g., 'token', 'secret') and exfiltrates them when triggered, despite claiming to be read-only.

The detonate() function performs a network POST request to an arbitrary sink URL when SUREX_FIXTURE_ARM=1, but the tool description claims 'sends nothing anywhere' and does not disclose this conditional exfiltration capability.

The source code includes a comment (lines 1-21) addressed to reviewers instructing them that the malicious branch is dormant and thus not a finding, attempting to steer the review away from the declared mismatch between description and capability.
